claim_boundary: Eight assignments are analyst-reviewed from captured official PDFs and structured notes; claims are not independent reproductions.

rows.title: HuBERT-VIC: Improving Noise-Robust Automatic Speech Recognition of Speech Foundation Model via Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization
rows.semantic_reasoning: VICReg constraints make noisy speech representations retain useful acoustic units before recognition.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: A recognizer trained on clean speech should still map noisy speech to words. Mechanism: HuBERT-VIC applies VICReg terms to noisy representations and compares masked prediction with regularizer ablations on MUSAN-noised LibriSpeech. Result: All three regularizers give the best reported WER and show complementary ablation effects. Boundary: MUSAN, SNR choices, HuBERT, and LibriSpeech bound the result; real conversational noise is not established.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: Accent Normalization Using Self-Supervised Discrete Tokens with Non-Parallel Data
rows.semantic_reasoning: Discrete tokens change pronunciation while preserving speaker identity with nonparallel accent data.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Accent normalization should change pronunciation while keeping the same speaker recognizable. Mechanism: The system extracts source tokens, predicts target-accent tokens, synthesizes waveform output, and evaluates several English accents. Result: The system beats a frame-to-frame baseline on naturalness, accentedness, and timbre preservation, but post-conversion WER remains high. Boundary: Accent definitions, targets, subjective judgments, and nonparallel training bound the claim; native-like is not universally better.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: Structured Codebook Based Hierarchical Framework for DNN for Computationally Efficient Speech Enhancement
rows.semantic_reasoning: Structured codebooks reduce enhancement cost by exploiting regularities in speech parameters.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Speech enhancement should run on a device that cannot afford a large neural network. Mechanism: Hierarchically clustered log-power-spectrum vectors drive codebook stages and enhancement predictors evaluated on VoiceBank-DEMAND. Result: The framework reduces computation while retaining comparable or improved enhancement scores over the reference systems. Boundary: One corpus and parameterized spectral targets bound the evidence; downstream ASR and perceptual benefit are not fully established.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: Spatio-Spectral Diarization of Meetings by Combining TDOA-based Segmentation and Speaker Embedding-based Clustering
rows.semantic_reasoning: TDOA and speaker embeddings combine room geometry with voice identity without equating position to identity.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Meeting transcription needs to know who spoke when despite overlap and movement. Mechanism: TDOA detects regions, embeddings assign speakers, cACGMM optionally refines them, and compact/distributed microphone setups are tested. Result: The combined pipeline outperforms single-channel pyannote in reported compact and distributed meeting scenarios. Boundary: Layouts, datasets, overlap, and spatial cues bound the result; evaluations are author-reported.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: Acoustic and Linguistic Biomarkers for Cognitive Impairment Detection from Speech
rows.semantic_reasoning: Class-aware acoustic and linguistic ensembles test cognitive-decline signals while exposing clinical data imbalance.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Speech may contain signs of cognitive decline, but health signals must be separated from topic and class imbalance. Mechanism: PROCESS Challenge systems combine acoustic features, text features, LLM descriptors, Longformer, ECAPA-TDNN, and TRILLsson embeddings across three tasks. Result: Selected ensembles provide the strongest reported balance across train/development data and individual classes. Boundary: Challenge data, demographic overlap, and missing metadata limit the claim; this is not clinical validation.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: DiEmo-TTS: Disentangled Emotion Representations via Self-Supervised Distillation for Cross-Speaker Emotion Transfer in Text-to-Speech
rows.semantic_reasoning: Disentangled emotion embeddings change delivery while protecting the target speaker's voice.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Emotion transfer should change delivery without replacing the target speaker's identity. Mechanism: DiEmo-TTS clusters emotion attributes, matches speaker/emotion examples, distills representations, and uses a dual-conditioning transformer. Result: The reported system improves emotion and speaker-related measures in the chosen experiments. Boundary: Pretrained encoders, datasets, subjective measures, and cross-speaker coverage bound the conclusion.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: Codec-Based Deepfake Source Tracing via Neural Audio Codec Taxonomy
rows.semantic_reasoning: Codec taxonomy makes fake-speech source tracing a provenance problem rather than only binary detection.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: Detecting fake speech says it is synthetic; tracing its source can explain which generator family produced it. Mechanism: Multi-task systems on CodecFake+ use codec quantization, auxiliary codec tasks, and balanced source-tracing experiments. Result: CodecFake+ gives initial evidence that codec taxonomy helps source tracing and that balance affects generalization. Boundary: The dataset and generator coverage bound the result; 46.45% F1 is not reliable attribution.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: Who Gets the Mic? Investigating Gender Bias in the Speaker Assignment of a Speech-LLM
rows.semantic_reasoning: Default speaker assignment makes social associations in speech generation observable as an accountability behavior.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: A speech model that chooses a voice can reveal social associations even when text does not request gender. Mechanism: Bark is prompted with two constructed datasets and assignments are counted for gender alignment and inclinations. Result: Bark shows gender awareness and some inclinations but no strong systematic bias under the tested prompts. Boundary: Two datasets, one model, prompt wording, and supported voices bound the conclusion; this is not a fairness guarantee.
